primary_responsibilities: Negotiating and executing media buys across channels—securing inventory at optimal CPMs/CPCs within approved budgets and ensuring campaign delivery against plan
Managing vendor and publisher relationships, including upfront negotiations, make-good policies, added value, and bonus impressions
Issuing insertion orders (IOs), managing IO revisions, and ensuring terms align with approved plans
Monitoring in-flight campaign delivery pacing and performance against contracted terms; identifying and resolving underdelivery issues
Reconciling media invoices against contracted delivery, flagging discrepancies, and managing billing approval workflows
Managing programmatic campaign execution within DSP platforms—building campaigns, setting up targeting, optimizing bids and budgets in real time
daily_tasks: Pulling and reviewing pacing reports from platforms and vendor partners; flagging campaigns running over or under budget
Responding to publisher and platform questions on live campaigns (creative swaps, schedule changes, technical issues)
Negotiating make-goods or credit adjustments for campaigns that underdelivered against contracted specs
Managing programmatic campaign optimizations—adjusting bids, updating audience segments, reviewing supply-path performance in DSP
Processing invoices and reconciling billing discrepancies against insertion orders in financial tracking systems
Communicating delivery and performance updates to media planners and account managers
tools_they_use: DSP platforms for programmatic execution (The Trade Desk, DV360, Amazon DSP, Xandr)
Platform-native buying interfaces (Google Ads, Meta Ads Manager, TikTok Ads, LinkedIn Campaign Manager)
Ad serving and trafficking systems (Google Campaign Manager 360, Sizmek/Amazon Ad Server)
Invoice and billing management systems (MediaLink, Advantage, or custom financial tracking spreadsheets)
IO and contract management tools (electronic signature platforms, vendor portals)
Competitive intelligence and rate benchmarking tools (MediaRadar, Kantar, internal rate card databases)
context.content_needs: Media buyers need practical, execution-focused content: negotiation guides and scripts for specific channel negotiations (upfront TV, programmatic PMP deals), IO templates and checklist frameworks, platform how-tos and setup guides (especially for new channels), CPM benchmark databases for negotiation preparation, billing reconciliation process guides, and glossaries of platform-specific terms and specs.
decision_criteria: Rate efficiency: Is the negotiated CPM/CPC at or below market rate, and does it compare favorably to plan estimates?
Inventory quality and delivery guarantee: Can the publisher/platform guarantee delivery of contracted impressions on schedule?
Vendor reliability and relationship history: Has this partner delivered on past commitments, handled make-goods professionally, and been a trustworthy partner?
Added value and bonus negotiation: What can be secured beyond the base buy—bonus impressions, content integrations, first-look deals?
Technical execution feasibility: Are the ad specs, tagging requirements, and creative deadlines achievable within campaign timelines?
Contractual terms and flexibility: Do cancellation terms, make-good policies, and contract flexibility match the client's needs?
pain_points: Invoice reconciliation is a constant time sink—billing discrepancies between what was ordered, what was delivered, and what the vendor invoiced require significant back-and-forth to resolve
Tracking hundreds of individual line items across dozens of vendors and platforms in manual spreadsheets is error-prone and time-inefficient
Publisher and platform account representatives have high turnover, requiring constant re-education of new contacts on account history and preferences
Make-good negotiations are contentious and time-consuming when vendors dispute delivery shortfalls or offer inadequate compensation
Programmatic transparency issues in open auction—media buyers cannot always verify that impressions ran where and when claimed, especially without ad verification tags
Rushed creative delivery from internal teams creates day-of-launch scrambles, trafficking delays, and potential missed campaign start dates
context.career_path: Assistant Media Buyer → Media Buyer → Senior Media Buyer → Associate Director, Buying / Investment → Director, Investment → VP, Investment → Chief Investment Officer / Head of Buying. Buyers can specialize by channel (TV buyer, digital/programmatic buyer, social buyer) or remain generalists. The programmatic specialty has become a distinct career track with demand for technical skills in DSP operation, audience data strategy, and supply-path optimization.
context.reports_to: Associate Director or Director of Investment / Buying (at agencies); Media Director or VP, Media (at in-house brands); Group Media Director (at large holding company agency networks)
collaborates_with: Media Planners (translates approved plans into executed buys; the planner-buyer handoff is the primary workflow interface)
Ad Operations / Trafficking team (coordinates ad serving setup, tag implementation, and creative specifications)
Analytics team (provides performance data context for buy optimization decisions)
Finance / Billing team (invoice approvals, budget reconciliation, vendor payment status)
Account Manager / Client Lead (escalates delivery issues or upsell opportunities that require client communication)
context.format_preferences: Process documentation and checklists are highly valued—buyers are execution-oriented and value standardized workflows. Platform-specific guides, IO templates, and negotiation prep sheets are the highest utility content. Rate benchmarking guides (to validate whether a negotiated rate is competitive) and channel spec sheets (ad formats, tagging requirements, creative deadlines) are regularly referenced. Buyers prefer concise, practical formats over conceptual frameworks.
